subject: The 7AM scan that saved her marriage
preview_text: How our top 1% of users catch patterns you're missing—and why they do it before coffee.
body_paragraphs: She woke up at 7AM, grabbed her phone, and scanned a 3-week-old text thread before her partner even stirred. Not because she was paranoid—because she knew something felt off but couldn't name it. That scan flagged four instances of gaslighting she'd normalized.

Here's what our top 1% of users do differently: they don't scan in the heat of an argument. They scan when they're calm, alone, and honest with themselves. They build a habit of reviewing patterns weekly, not just when something blows up. It's like checking your smoke detector batteries—boring until it saves your life.

Your app already has a pattern detection feature that tracks toxicity across every conversation you've scanned. But most people only use it reactively. Power users open the Relationship Health Dashboard every Sunday night, look at their toxicity trend line, and ask one question: 'Am I getting safer or numb to this?'

Open Red Flag Scanner AI right now and check your pattern history. If your toxicity score has stayed flat for two weeks, you might be missing something. P.S. The average user who reviews their dashboard weekly catches red flags 6 days earlier than those who don't.
